questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good study environment, interesting classes and a fitting schedule.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to check-in to the university, but more difficult to find the digital platforms where important information was displayed. It took a while to get to know how the app for uni Milan works and therefore being able to check where and when there were classes. A bit confusing platforms.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Hmm not much, we could write to the mobility office for help, but otherwise we as fellow exchange students used each other a lot for figuring things out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Not any orientation :)

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult. We had an airbnb and where luccky to later on find an apartment that we could rent while we where there. It is definitly easier finding housing alone than as a group, but check the different websites and be careful of scammers.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Look for housing close to convenient public transport. The metro is most stable and on time, but it closes at night, whereas the trams are generally less dependable, but they drive at night, so it is possible to come home.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Difficult to find something available and feeling secure about paying, but i had friends who booked from home though an agency and it worked out great.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, it is in person, so expect a line, but no problems with this. You show up at the international office and wait in line, then you go in and give your passport and your information and a document is made for you. that's it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not really any... asking around?

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't end up taking the classes i thought from home, but i was happy with by classes. You get to try out classes you are interested in for a while, because you only have to register to classes right before registering to the exams of the classes. But the curriculum starts from the first week, so you will risk missing some things by "shopping around".

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Patience and it will work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses levels are quite different from courses at KU. You are expected a bit more to say something, because some classes are very small (10 people or so). The masters levels where fine for a lot of us on the bachelor. The exams are a bit more elaborate, i had 2 written assignments that had to be between 15 and 20 pages. And the oral exams require you to read a lot. But the exams where fine to be at.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Almost no group work, more seminars and class discussions. A lot less critical thinking which was interesting...

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Western tradition: political and moral values. (philosophy)
Intellectuals, popular culture, collective identities: Italy and Europe in the 19th and 20th centuries (history)
Biopolitics: bodies, health and food (philosophy).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Biopolitics was personally very interesting to me and the classes where very chill. 
Intellectuals was a lot about italian history and with a cultural history angle, so if this is interesting for you take that.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Expensive fee for a real estate agent showing us an apartment.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries where the same as denmark, so a bit expensive. Coffee was vey cheap. Eating out was also cheeper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None that i knew of really, but check the student mail, there might be some offers that i missed.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Aperitivos with classmates after class.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
On warm days going to lake como. The tickets are cheap and it takes under 2 hours and it is so beautiful. Go to a beach there and take the ferry around the lake. 
Going to Genova to see the coast and swim. 
Trains are generally cheap and pretty easy to get around with.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Even though it is a fast paced city, the feeling is chill.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn some italian and be friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Italian bureaucracy... It was horrible getting wifi and cancelling it, it took 8 trips to the wifi-store and felt impossible...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cheap coffee and aperitivo (meeting for a drink and a snack after school/work, before dinner). And a general politeness and curtesy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Classes will most likely be on different campuses around the city. 
Get a travel card (will save you money) 
Learn some polite italian frases.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It will work out, the host institution is very chill.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Passing the exams and getting to know locals in my neighborhood.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Our living situation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
